finding: Both provide source-backed retrieval/navigation. Knowledge Experience is a broad generated human/machine entry layer; Task172 adds bounded facet routing, explicit fallback and exact-ID validation. They are overlapping consumers, not duplicate registries.

maintenance_cost.why: Separate generators/facets and source fingerprints require synchronized contracts.

cognitive_load.why: Readers may mistake search, facet routing and method selection as one operation.

migration_risk.why: Collapsing them can break Knowledge projections, exact-ID fallback and Task179 fixture provenance.

deletion_risk.why: The index is a referenced Task179 baseline/fixture surface; deletion would remove a bounded routing contract.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; document the handoff from broad retrieval to exact-ID bounded routing.
unresolved: No unified source-level relation says when an asset becomes a method-use candidate.

finding: All contain typed IDs, provenance, evidence/uncertainty or boundaries, but Foundation registries adjudicate canonical asset/claim identity while Cognitive IR is a provisional method/object carrier. Shared fields do not mean shared authority or state machine.

maintenance_cost.why: Repeated field vocabularies can drift even while semantics differ.

cognitive_load.why: Names such as object, claim, status and ceiling invite accidental cross-namespace reasoning.

migration_risk.why: Merging would risk claim promotion, identity collision or silent loss of a source-specific ceiling.

deletion_risk.why: Foundation registries are canonical; R0 references them as protected authorities.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; retain explicit provenance-only references and namespace-qualified types.
unresolved: Cross-version adapters need an explicit non-promotion and unknown-preservation test.

finding: Failure taxonomies, operational memory and self-correction all retain failures or repairs; self-correction additionally derives changed-claim/dependency/evidence impacts and remediation, while runtime memory supports bounded operational recall and rollback.

maintenance_cost.why: Multiple owners, schemas and retention policies must remain aligned without forcing one store.

cognitive_load.why: Failure, rollback, remediation and recurrence can be confused as interchangeable records.

migration_risk.why: Consolidation could mix canonical claim review with sensitive/run-scoped operational memory.

deletion_risk.why: History, recurrence and rollback lineage can be irrecoverable once discarded.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; share provenance and cross-reference IDs, not retention or authority.
unresolved: No evidence shows a common recurrence ontology across repository and runtime memory.

finding: Both use correction/change language. Self-correction is a deterministic repository delta/impact/remediation projection; a cognitive transition is an explicit candidate record of reframing and method disposition. Neither proves the other occurred.

maintenance_cost.why: Shared words tempt redundant fields, but separate contracts are currently understandable.

cognitive_load.why: Users can conflate fixing a generated projection with revising a reasoning method.

migration_risk.why: A shared status machine would blur claim governance and research-only cognitive records.

deletion_risk.why: Removing either erases a distinct audit trail or candidate transition contract.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; link a transition to a relevant remediation event only with exact provenance.
unresolved: No tested adapter maps a self-correction event to a cognitive transition.

finding: Method/unknown/boundary/lineage terms recur across a summary self-model, object graph and event transition. Their intended grains differ (whole-system declaration, persistent object/relation, transition event), but field ownership and references need to remain explicit.

maintenance_cost.why: Repeated fields can require synchronized schema/version/validator edits.

cognitive_load.why: Three artifacts can appear to restate the same method and unknowns.

migration_risk.why: Shared refs permit adapters, but collapsing grains could make transition history overwrite a self-model snapshot.

deletion_risk.why: Some duplicated summaries may be compressible only after consumers and reconstruction tests are known.

recommended_disposition: NEEDS_ADJUDICATION; preserve current schemas; next evidence should trace field-level consumer/reference use across fixtures.
unresolved: Consumer-level normalization has not been independently demonstrated.

finding: Task179 package defines roles, frozen criteria, blind-first order and write surfaces. Task181 defines how resulting evidence is typed, hashed and excluded from shared discovery. They operate at evaluation design versus post-production admission.

maintenance_cost.why: Criteria/schema and shared admission policy must evolve together across rounds.

cognitive_load.why: Their distinct stages are legible when package and evidence lifecycle are linked.

migration_risk.why: Changing the evaluation output path without changing admission rules can reopen a discovery path.

deletion_risk.why: Removing isolation can backflow evaluator material; removing the package eliminates frozen roles/criteria.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_BOTH; bind evaluator output schemas to admission receipts and exact source hashes.
unresolved: Task185 did not run or assess evaluator independence.

finding: Path accounting validates category coverage and anti-backflow; R0 schema validates package shape/role contracts; Task181 admission policy excludes evaluation artifacts from specified discovery consumers. They touch adjacent boundary concerns but have different input domains and invariants.

maintenance_cost.why: Shared path/category changes must propagate to admission tests and package references.

cognitive_load.why: Several validators can be mistaken for one comprehensive correctness gate.

migration_risk.why: Combining validators could create bypasses or shift authority from a local consumer to a generic checker.

deletion_risk.why: Each guards a distinct repository surface; no equivalent replacement evidence exists.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; document which validator owns each invariant and add cross-layer contract tests only where paths meet.
unresolved: A cross-layer test matrix for every generated/discovery consumer is outside this research step.

finding: All describe capabilities, but existing registries scope runtime/executor/provider operations; R0 describes cognitive artifact serialization, transition and successor reconstruction and explicitly leaves calibration unmeasured. Similar labels conceal different consumers and evidence.

maintenance_cost.why: Crosswalks and shared capability vocabulary need version updates.

cognitive_load.why: A single 'capability' word spans permissions, executable operations and model competence.

migration_risk.why: Merging could make an interface or permission request look like measured competence.

deletion_risk.why: Both are referenced by runtime and R0 fixtures; their consumers differ.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; use qualified capability namespaces and explicit evidence-state fields.
unresolved: No cross-provider cognitive calibration record is present.

finding: Decision Integrity freezes principles/order/risks/stop conditions before outcomes; M0/M1 sketches and adjudicates mechanism paths and alternatives; 121Q16 records bounded alternatives/affordable loss. They touch decisions but answer different questions and are not one causal-scale allocator.

maintenance_cost.why: Templates can drift across decision and mechanism records.

cognitive_load.why: Ex-ante process quality, mechanism evidence and action selection are adjacent but distinct.

migration_risk.why: A shared schema could lose either principled decision order or causal test fields.

deletion_risk.why: Historical candidate records and current mechanism docs are useful for separate audits.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; map explicit handoff fields only after comparing task families.
unresolved: No controlled comparison shows whether either decision contract scales effort by causal reach, reversibility or duration.

finding: 'Observation' names at least an external-interface exposure/signal ledger, bounded local process-observation reconciliation, and statistical/partial-observation model state. Task140 expressly disclaims world-truth sensing. Treating these as one feedback sensor would be a semantic collapse.

maintenance_cost.why: Common vocabulary needs types and boundaries at handoffs.

cognitive_load.why: The word suggests one sensor despite distinct observers, domains and claim ceilings.

migration_risk.why: Unifying could falsely promote local process evidence to world truth or calibration.

deletion_risk.why: The ledgers and typed outcome history are needed to preserve non-equivalence and exposure boundaries.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; use observation-kind, observer-frame and claim-ceiling fields at any future federation point.
unresolved: No shared typed observation relation binds the three domains.

finding: Historical audit/retrieval artifacts generate candidate mappings and non-correspondence residue; Foundation's isomorphism gate constrains what may be claimed. No proof that Q37/Q38 were adopted or that the present gate reproduces their pilot.

maintenance_cost.why: Historical lab contracts and current canonical gate evolve on separate clocks.

cognitive_load.why: Candidate analogy search can be confused with proof of structure preservation.

migration_risk.why: Bulk migration could promote research candidates or discard negative-transfer residues.

deletion_risk.why: Historical artifacts preserve failure/negative-transfer provenance even if not active.

recommended_disposition: KEEP_SEPARATE; reuse only via a provenance-bound adapter after a behavior-level comparison.
unresolved: Archived lab bodies were not exhaustively re-read for all downstream consumers.

finding: The current governance document explicitly marks the 2026-07-09 meta-protocol→function→case hierarchy as superseded as an exhaustive architecture and keeps its rows historical. Task179's typed cognitive substrate is a narrower new purpose; it does not restore that hierarchy or claim the whole repository is a single cognitive registry.

maintenance_cost.why: Current mapping and historical lineage are documented in one architecture source.

cognitive_load.why: Old vocabulary persists in dated assets and can be mistaken for current ontology.

migration_risk.why: Bulk renaming/reclassification would erase dated identity and adjudication lineage.

deletion_risk.why: The source expressly retains old records as history; deletion would remove provenance and withdrawn-claim evidence.

recommended_disposition: PRESERVE_HISTORICAL_ONLY labels; do not reactivate the old exhaustive architecture without a separate adjudication.
unresolved: No exact abandoned-path reactivation was found in the inspected Task179–181 lineage; the broader repository search is not a proof of absence.
